title: Trump Says US Will Raise Canada Auto, Parts, and Steel Tariffs to 50% on Jan. 1, 2027
detail: President Trump announced on Truth Social on Monday, August 24, 2026 that tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel would rise to 50% effective January 1, 2027, doubling the current 25% rate applied to non-US content, and declaring 'Canada will be treated like a State no longer.' The threat follows the collapse of US-Canada trade talks on August 21 and the 50% tariffs already in effect on roughly $20 billion of other Canadian goods; Trump accused Canada of 'ripping off the United States of America for years.' Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has vowed to retaliate 'dollar for dollar,' with Canada's countermeasures targeting US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper, and electronics starting September 8.

media.caption: Trump says US auto, parts, and steel tariffs on Canada will rise to 50% on Jan. 1, 2027

title: Bessent Unveils 'Economic D-Day' Sanctions Against Iran, Iran Warns of Hormuz Ship Seizures
detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled a sweeping new round of economic measures against Iran on Monday, August 24, 2026, branded by Bessent and Trump as an 'economic D-Day' and described by Bessent as 'the single greatest financial offensive ever.' Writing in the Financial Times, Bessent said the goal was to 'sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,' with the sanctions aimed at foreign governments and entities — particularly China, which buys roughly 90% of Iran's oil exports — that continue trading with Tehran. Iran's currency has plunged to a record low and inflation is near 90%. Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, warned of 'seismic' retaliation and threatened to seize ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz in violation of Iranian rules if neighboring countries join the sanctions push.

media.caption: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveils new 'economic D-Day' sanctions against Iran

title: Supreme Court Gives Trump Preliminary Win on Mail-In Voting Restrictions
detail: The Supreme Court, divided 6-3 along ideological lines, lifted on Monday, August 24, 2026 a Massachusetts-based judge's June injunction that had blocked key provisions of Trump's March 2026 executive order restricting mail-in voting from taking effect this year in California and 22 other states. The unsigned majority opinion found the states' challenge premature since the order had not yet been enforced; Justices Jackson, Sotomayor, and Kagan dissented. The order directs DHS to compile citizenship lists for each state, instructs the Attorney General to prioritize prosecuting officials who issue ballots to ineligible voters, and requires the Postal Service to withhold ballots from voters not on official enrollment lists. The ruling is narrow — a separate lower-court order still blocks the plan in full — but hands Trump momentum weeks before officials begin mailing midterm ballots.

media.caption: The Supreme Court lifts an injunction blocking Trump's mail-in voting restrictions in 23 states

title: Secret Service Confirms Iranian State Media Video Threatening Barron Trump
detail: The US Secret Service confirmed Monday, August 24, 2026 it is aware of a nearly three-minute video aired by Iranian state television — reportedly linked to IRGC-affiliated media — titled 'Where to Kill Barron Trump,' which claimed a $10 million bounty and referenced locations including his place of study and Trump Tower in New York. Secret Service spokesman Nate Herring said the agency 'investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees' but declined further comment 'out of concern for operational security.' The video follows a similar July threat against First Lady Melania Trump and Iranian state media's repeated targeting of the Trump family since the US and Israel killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in February 2026; it is the first time Barron has been publicly singled out.

media.caption: Secret Service confirms it is aware of an Iranian state media video threatening Barron Trump's life
